blockers: legal or policy limits on release
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Release remains uncertain because the scenario does not guarantee timing, completeness, or scope.
endpoint_ledger.description: The controversy reaches a terminal informational state where body-camera footage or equivalent authoritative context is publicly available and materially clarifies the encounter.
endpoint_ledger.label: Public release of clarifying context

meta.important_question: Will materially clarifying body-camera footage or equivalent full-context evidence become public within the scenario window?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This is a core terminal information outcome because it can decisively alter what later actors can claim.
realization_criteria: Agency publicly releases body-camera footage, extended footage, or an authoritative detailed reconstruction
Released material materially resolves at least one central ambiguity of the edited clip
Reporters or major public channels reference the released context as primary evidence
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Scenario explicitly states the agency can release body-camera footage after privacy review, but full footage is unavailable at T0.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Persistence is plausible but not certain; a strong corrective information cascade could prevent dominance.
endpoint_ledger.description: The early edited-clip interpretation stays socially dominant or persistently influential despite verification efforts or later corrections.
endpoint_ledger.label: Edited clip narrative remains entrenched

meta.important_question: Will the edited clip remain the dominant public narrative even after verification efforts begin?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario is about misinformation dynamics, so persistence of false or incomplete framing is a principal endpoint.
realization_criteria: Majority of high-visibility public discussion continues citing the original clip framing after verification attempts
Correction content receives lower sustained engagement than original outrage content
Rumor repetition persists across influencer or public channels after clarifying evidence appears or is reported absent
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Scenario explicitly warns that rumors may persist after correction, making narrative entrenchment a live endpoint.

blockers: visible privacy rationale accepted as legitimate
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A careful but timely response could keep the issue in a procedural evidence lane rather than a coverup lane.
endpoint_ledger.description: The main public interpretation shifts from the officer's conduct alone to a broader belief that the agency is hiding or managing evidence illegitimately.
endpoint_ledger.label: Agency response collapses into coverup framing

meta.important_question: Will the transit agency preserve enough legitimacy to keep the controversy procedural rather than being cast as a coverup?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Decision authority over release creates leverage, but also reputational exposure if the process is perceived as evasive.
realization_criteria: Public-facing discourse prominently accuses the agency of concealment or bad-faith delay
Agency statements are widely treated as illegitimate or untrustworthy by rider and online audiences
Calls for external oversight or pressure escalate primarily because of the response process rather than only the original clip
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: The agency has asymmetric evidence control and procedural delay constraints, creating a live risk of delegitimation at T0.

blockers: faster viral recirculation of the edited clip
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Even strong reporting may not fully dominate if audiences prefer identity-consistent clip narratives.
endpoint_ledger.description: Investigative reporting becomes the main trusted lens through which the public interprets the incident, reducing dependence on the raw viral clip.
endpoint_ledger.label: Reporter-mediated reframing becomes dominant

meta.important_question: Will investigative reporting measurably shift audience attention from raw outrage to evidence-based interpretation?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This endpoint captures whether verification intermediaries can materially redirect information dynamics.
realization_criteria: Reporter outputs become the most-cited sources in subsequent public discussion
Public conversations increasingly reference verification status, missing context, or reported factual findings
Influencer and rider-group narratives adapt to reporter-established evidence boundaries
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Reporters are explicitly present as verification actors, but their success depends on access and timing.

risk_flags.note: Agency-controlled footage creates asymmetric access to truth at T0.
Edited visual evidence can generate strong belief before verification.
Privacy review slows correction relative to amplification speed.
Scenario explicitly indicates rumors may persist after correction.
Initializer should avoid assuming the officer is clearly guilty or exonerated at T0.

simulation_brief.horizon_notes: Short-cycle information cascade with institutional review lag
simulation_brief.summary: An edited video appears to show a transit officer insulting riders, but full footage is unavailable at T0. Rider groups, transit police, local influencers, and investigative reporters react under uncertainty. The transit agency may release body-camera footage only after privacy review. Influencers can amplify claims but cannot independently verify the underlying event. Rumors may persist after later correction.
time_zero_conditions: Full footage is not publicly available
Formal correction mechanism exists through agency review and possible body-camera release
Public attention is likely to outpace verified evidence
uncertainty_notes: Clip authenticity as a complete representation of the encounter is unverified
Officer conduct severity is unclear without full footage
Agency response speed depends on privacy review process
Persistence of belief after correction is plausible

sociology_baseline.note: People may accept updates that fit existing beliefs about authority or rider mistreatment
Visible peer concern can move accountability demands from discussion to coordinated action
Some actors privately dissent from the dominant public clip narrative but speak cautiously
Accounts cluster into communities that repeat aligned interpretations
Repeated exposure from multiple visible accounts can harden belief in the edited clip framing
Group loyalties shape interpretation of accountability and procedural fairness
Attention may fall quickly unless refreshed by new evidence, official action, or controversy

sociology_prompt_influences.description: An edited clip creates a salient but incomplete visual narrative that encourages overconfident interpretation
Official evidence release is slower than social amplification because privacy review is required
The agency holds potential clarifying footage while outside actors lack direct access
Some audiences may continue repeating early claims after later clarification
Influencers can magnify attention without resolving factual uncertainty
